$comment: Only servers verified as real in MCP_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md are listed here. Every entry needs a real API key/token in the env var shown before it will work — none are pre-filled. Never commit real secrets into this file; use your shell environment or a .env loaded outside version control. Review each server's source/README yourself before enabling it for a client engagement.

ahrefs.$comment: Ahrefs recommends their remote MCP over this local package (see verification report). Local package requires an API v3 key, not an MCP key.

brevo.$comment: Free-tier alternative to Klaviyo for clients who can't cover a paid subscription. Official Brevo-published remote MCP (developers.brevo.com/docs/mcp-protocol). A first account hit a hard, reproducible bug: OAuth authorization succeeded but every actual API call returned 401 (likely because the OAuth consent screen only requested identity scopes -- openid/email/profile -- not a data-access scope). A second, separate Brevo account's token connected cleanly with zero issues (no OAuth prompt even needed, Bearer token alone worked) -- confirming this is account-specific (plan/permission flag), not a bug in Brevo's MCP implementation itself. If this fails for a given account: try regenerating the key, confirm the account's plan actually includes API/MCP access, and if it still fails, a fresh account is a working fallback. Free plan has historically included ~300 emails/day, unlimited contacts -- verify current limits on Brevo's pricing page. Generate the token at Brevo -> Account -> SMTP & API -> API Keys -> create a key with the 'MCP option' enabled.

canva.$comment: Official Canva remote MCP, bridged locally via mcp-remote. Auth happens via interactive OAuth, not a static key.

google-analytics.$comment: Community server (ruchernchong/mcp-server-google-analytics), not Google-published. Verified by running it directly: it requires GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL, GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY, GA_PROPERTY_ID exactly (not the Google-standard GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS/GA4_PROPERTY_ID names originally assumed here).

google-sheets.$comment: Community server (freema/mcp-gsheets), not Google-published. Verified by running it directly: it wants GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY as the raw JSON string (or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS as a file path, or GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY+GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL) — the GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON name originally used here isn't recognized by this package.

google-ads.$comment: Switched from @samihalawa/google-ads-mcp-server after runtime testing found a published syntax error (server.js:915, breaks regardless of credentials). @zleventer/google-ads-mcp tested clean (no crash on startup). Requires GOOGLE_ADS_CUSTOMER_ID (target account, no dashes) and optionally GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID (manager account ID, only if the target is a linked client account under a manager). Re-verify current maintainer/version before granting spend-affecting scopes.

saleshandy.$comment: Cheaper alternative to Instantly (~$25/mo, 7-day free trial). The published repo (ftaxats/SHMCP) is NOT a runnable stdio server as-is -- it's packaged for Smithery's cloud hosting (config injected via their runtime, no env-var entry point) and its compiled dist/ output was also missing required .js extensions on relative ESM imports, causing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Node. Both issues were fixed locally: cloned to C:\Users\Tech\mcp-servers\SHMCP, patched the compiled import paths, and added a custom stdio-entry.mjs that calls the exported createServer() directly with env-var config and connects it to a real StdioServerTransport. Verified working end-to-end (all 9 tools registered) with a placeholder key. Source reviewed: base URL defaults to the real api.saleshandy.com, no unexpected endpoints. Only 9 tools (campaigns/templates/contacts), no lead-search -- pair with Apollo/Hunter for sourcing.

smartlead.$comment: Cheaper alternative to Instantly ($39/mo, 14-day free trial with 2,500 email credits). Built by LeadMagic, an official SmartLead partner -- verified working directly via npx with no fixes needed: 49/113+ tools load by default, and it correctly rejected a placeholder key with a real 401 rather than silently accepting bad input. Set SMARTLEAD_ADVANCED_TOOLS=true and/or SMARTLEAD_ADMIN_TOOLS=true (as additional env vars) to unlock more of the 113+ tool set if needed.

instantly.$comment: Verified via runtime testing: this package ignores INSTANTLY_API_KEY as an env var entirely and requires the key as a --api-key CLI argument instead.

b2b-enrichment.$comment: Single-maintainer Python project (Aleksey-Panf/b2b-enrichment-mcp). Source reviewed: only calls api.apollo.io and api.hunter.io, no unexpected endpoints. Installed in its own venv at C:\Users\Tech\mcp-servers\b2b-enrichment-mcp (outside this repo). Its pyproject.toml pins 'mcp[cli]>=1.9.0' with no upper bound, which pulled in an incompatible mcp 2.0.0 by default (removed the fastmcp submodule this code needs) — the venv has 'mcp[cli]<2.0' pinned instead (installed 1.29.0). Real module path is apollo_mcp.server, not b2b_enrichment_mcp as originally assumed.

socialneuron.$comment: Requires a paid Social Neuron plan (Pro Trial is NOT sufficient per their own dashboard). Verified via runtime testing: a bare 'npx @socialneuron/mcp-server' fails with 'could not determine executable to run' (no matching bin), so the package name needs an explicit -p bin flag. The documented 'login' subcommand is broken as of v2.0.1 and v1.9.0 — it claims to wait for an OAuth callback but never opens a local listening port (confirmed via direct process/network inspection), so it can never succeed. Working alternative: generate an API key directly from the Social Neuron web dashboard (Developers -> API Keys) and set it as SOCIALNEURON_API_KEY — the server does honor that env var despite it not being the documented primary auth path.

$notWired.$comment: See MCP_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md. These require an API/account with per-call billing or a remote-only setup, so they're documented in agency-assets/mcp-configurations/ instead of pre-wired here: Forage MCP (Apify pay-per-call), Hunter.io (official remote MCP, no local package), Lamina (github.com/uselamina/lamina-mcp, requires its own hosted API key).
